title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: elliptic curves E/S over S above S_0 = Spec Z[1/2], with Legendre-type rigidifications that Grothendieck calls 'épi-glyphes'.

1. Jacobi épi-glyphes of order 2. These are orderings of the three nonzero 2-torsion points. They form the sections of an (S_3)_S-torsor, with S_3 = GL_2(F_2) acting by permuting the points.

2. Legendre épi-glyphes. On the previous page these form a torsor under H_4 (identified with mu_4). Its associated mu_2-torsor is canonically omega_J ∧ mu_4^*.

3. 'Bi-glyphes'. A bi-glyphe is a pair consisting of an ordering of E[2] and a Legendre rigidification. Bi-glyphes form a torsor under (mu_4 × S_3)_S, formula (45).

4. Fine moduli scheme. By (37) the bi-glyphe problem is represented by U_{0,3} ×_{S_0} mu_4^*.
 - U_{0,3} = P^1_{S_0} minus {0,1,∞} is the Legendre λ-line.
 - mu_4^* is the scheme of primitive 4th roots of unity, i.e. Spec Z[1/2][i].
 - Hence the structure group mu_4 × S_3 acts on this scheme. Grothendieck says this action should be made explicit, together with the action on the line bundle Π_0 = O(1) on U_{0,3} × mu_4^* (46). This bundle presumably carries the Hodge/omega-type data.

5. The action (47).
 - S_3 acts on U_{0,3} 'tautologically'. U_{0,3} is viewed as the projective line of the 2-dimensional sum-zero part of O^{{0,1,∞}}, minus the three marked points. This gives the anharmonic action λ ↦ 1-λ, 1/λ, ….
 - S_3 acts on mu_4^* through the sign character (i ↦ i^{sg(g)}). This is needed because, for example, λ ↦ 1-λ requires y ↦ iy in y² = x(x-1)(x-λ).
 - mu_4 acts trivially on U_{0,3} and on mu_4^* through ζ ↦ ζ^2 ∈ {±1}.
 - So S_3 × mu_4 acts on mu_4^* via the mixed character sg(g)·ζ^2 (next page).

6. Next page. The stabiliser of mu_4^* is D'_3 = S_3 ×_{mu_2} mu_4, of order 12. Over S̃_0 = mu_4^* (i chosen) it becomes constant, a non-split central extension 1 → ±1 → D'_3 → S_3 → 1. This is the dicyclic (binary dihedral) group of order 12.

Purpose: present the moduli stack of elliptic curves over Z[1/2] as an explicit quotient of the Legendre/λ-line (times mu_4^*) by an explicit finite group, keeping track of the automorphism ±1 and of the arithmetic of i = sqrt(-1).
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page is a programme ('qu'il faudrait expliciter'): the action on Π_0 = O(1) is announced but not computed here.
Notation: mu_4^* is the scheme of primitive 4th roots, a mu_2-torsor rather than a group. 'Action via ζ^2' should be read as multiplication of the primitive root by ζ^2 = ±1, which is consistent.

ideas.what: Orderings of E[2] form an S_3-torsor; the λ-line U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞} carries the anharmonic S_3-action, realised through the action on the 2-dimensional sum-zero part of O^{{0,1,∞}}
ideas.modern_name: Full level-2 structure; Legendre λ-line as M(2); anharmonic group action
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi, Klein); scheme-theoretic: Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions M_{0,4} and M_{1,1} and their relation, but not this computation

ideas.what: Combined rigidification ('bi-glyphe': level-2 ordering plus Legendre rigidification) forming a mu_4 × S_3 torsor, with moduli scheme U_{0,3} × mu_4^* over Z[1/2]
ideas.modern_name: Legendre moduli problem (rigidified level structure) and its representability
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Mazur (Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves, 1985), Igusa

ideas.what: Action of S_3 × mu_4 on the moduli scheme through the mixed character sg(g)·ζ^2 on mu_4^*; the stabiliser is S_3 ×_{mu_2} mu_4, a non-split extension of S_3 by ±1 (dicyclic group of order 12)
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2] as a quotient stack of the Legendre line; binary dihedral group of order 12
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (quotient-stack presentations of M_{1,1}; the Legendre family needing sqrt(-1))

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard scheme-theoretic treatment of the Legendre family and the S_3 symmetry of the λ-line. The extra mu_4^* factor tracks sqrt(-1). Grothendieck's idiosyncratic 'épi-glyphe' vocabulary is the only unusual element. The content (a presentation of M_{1,1} over Z[1/2] via the λ-line and a binary dihedral group of order 12) is known to specialists, for instance through Katz–Mazur and Legendre-moduli folklore.
transcription_corrections: 'Dans les bi-quadratiques' should read 'Donc les bi-glyphes' (the bi-glyphes forming the sections of a torsor).
'groupe [-constant-]' in line 4: 'constant' is struck through, consistent with (45) being written with subscript S.
In (47) 'la correction Sg(g)' is most likely 'la caractère/action sg(g)' (sign character), consistent with the next page's 'caractère mixte sg(g).ζ^2'.
'la can. corr.' is probably 'via la can. corr. mu_4 → mu_2 = {±1}_{S_0}', i.e. the canonical homomorphism ζ ↦ ζ^2.
'Σ_{0,1,∞}' is probably P_{{0,1,∞}}, the projective line built from V_{{0,1,∞}}(O_{S_0}).
Formula number before 'U_{0,3} ×_{S_0} mu_4^*' reads '(37)', referring back to an earlier formula.
